Read-only analysis in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Change nothing.

GOAL: Harvest the PROCESS and GOVERNANCE knowledge a frontend development lead on this project needs. This feeds a personal playbook, so I want the operative rules and the reasoning behind them — not a table of contents.

Cover these five areas. For each, read the actual source files and report what is true TODAY, flagging anything that looks stale or contradicted.

1. **Release, tagging and environment promotion.** Read .claude/rules/tagging.md and .docs/releaseBranchesRules.md in full, plus .github/workflows/deploy-*.yml and scripts/versionGuard.mjs. Report: the branch model, the tag taxonomy and who may cut each, the six environments and how each is deployed (continuous vs tag-promoted), the version guard's behaviour, and the rollback paths. Flag every place a workflow file disagrees with the docs.

2. **Protection tiers and approval.** Read .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md, .claude/rules/protectedFiles.md, and CODEOWNERS. Report: what makes a file Tier 1 vs Tier 2, who owns each group, how approval is actually enforced (server-side vs advisory), and — importantly — any path where CODEOWNERS and the rules files disagree. Note that CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, and check whether any intended rule is silently overridden by a later line.

3. **PR and review workflow.** Read coderabbit.yaml, .coderabbit/ (all rule files), semgrep.yml, and .github/workflows/qa.yml. Report: what is mechanically enforced at PR time vs advisory, which checks are required vs optional, and what a developer must do that no tool will catch for them.

4. **Sprint, story and Jira/Confluence workflow.** Read .docs/memory/sprintScope.md, .docs/memory/projectState.md, and any .claude/skills/ that relate to Jira, Confluence, story generation, or QA. Report the story decomposition convention, how work is scoped to a sprint, and any documented Confluence page structure.

5. **Integration and vendor boundaries.** List every file in .docs/integration/ with a one-line summary of the system it covers and who owns it. Note which integrations are live vs planned.

For each area, end with a short "what bites you" list — the specific, non-obvious traps a lead would hit. Report as structured markdown with file:line references. Be explicit about what you could not determine.

- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# Release & Hotfix Branch Rules
     2	
     3	**Read this file in full before taking any action when `git branch --show-current` matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`.** These rules apply *in addition to* the Hard Rules in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). On `feature/*` and `fix/*` branches they do not apply and this file can be ignored.
     4	
     5	See the branch table in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules for which branch merges where.
     6	
     7	## Back-merge rules (GitFlow)
     8	
     9	To prevent `develop` drifting from production:
    10	- When a `release/*` branch is merged to `main` at go-live, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
    11	- When a `hotfix/*` is merged to `main`, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
    12	- When a `fix/release-*` is merged into its `release/*` parent and the release later ships, the forward-merge to `develop` happens as part of the release back-merge above — no separate action.
    13	
    14	## Release Branch Behaviour
    15	
    16	When on a `release/*` branch, the following rules apply in addition to all Hard Rules.
    17	
    18	**Before writing any code, always:**
    19	1. State a plan — which files will change, what will change in each, and why.
    20	2. Assess blast radius — how many components, hooks, or pages consume each file being changed? Flag explicitly if any file has more than 3 consumers or is Tier 2 or above.
    21	3. Wait for explicit developer confirmation before making any edit, including trivial ones.
    22	
    23	**Allowed on release branches:**
    24	- Read-only skills: `/generate-changelog`, `/pr-checklist`, `/code-quality`
    25	- Trivial non-code changes (copy corrections, version bumps, feature flag toggles) — plan + confirm required
    26	- Code logic fixes — only on a `fix/release-{version}_{description}` sub-branch, never directly on the release branch
    27	
    28	**Not allowed on release branches:**
    29	- New features or scope additions not in the release
    30	- Refactoring
    31	- Dependency changes
    32	- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches
    33	
    34	**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**
    35	
    36	The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.
    37	
    38	```bash
    39	# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
    40	git checkout release/v0.1.0
    41	git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description
    42	
    43	# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
    44	gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
    45	```
    46	The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (when CI lands). See [architecture.md > Environments](architecture.md) for the full environment topology (Local · Dev · Test · SIT · UAT · Stage · Prod).

    29	- New features or scope additions not in the release
    30	- Refactoring
    31	- Dependency changes
    32	- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches
    33	
    34	**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**
    35	
    36	The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.
    37	
    38	```bash
    39	# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
    40	git checkout release/v0.1.0
    41	git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description
    42	
    43	# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
    44	gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
    45	```
    46	The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (when CI lands). See [architecture.md > Environments](architecture.md) for the full environment topology (Local · Dev · Test · SIT · UAT · Stage · Prod).

1	/**
     2	 * versionGuard.mjs — downgrade protection for tag-based environment promotion.
     3	 *
     4	 * On the GitHub Team plan, a deploy's auto-created Deployment records the *trigger*
     5	 * ref (the default branch), NOT the tag that was actually deployed. So we record the
     6	 * deployed tag ourselves (an explicit GitHub Deployment) and read it back here to
     7	 * block accidental downgrades on the manually-promoted tiers (test/uat/staging/prod).
     8	 *
     9	 * Usage (from a deploy-*.yml, after `npm install`, with GH_TOKEN set):
    10	 *   node scripts/versionGuard.mjs check  <env> <ref>   # before push — block a downgrade
    11	 *   node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record <env> <ref>   # after a successful push — record the tag
    12	 *
    13	 * <env> is the GitHub Environment name (test | uat | staging | prod).
    14	 *
    15	 * `check` behaviour:
    16	 *   - <ref> is not a version tag       -> skip/allow (e.g. deploying a feature branch to Test)
    17	 *   - <ref> not valid semver           -> fail closed (exit 1)
    18	 *   - no prior tag on the env          -> allow (first deploy)
    19	 *   - <ref> strictly older             -> BLOCK (exit 1)
    20	 *   - <ref> equal or newer             -> allow
    21	 *   - lookup error / invalid stored ref -> fail closed (exit 1)
    22	 *
    23	 * `record` skips non-version-tag refs; it FAILS the run if it cannot create the deployment record
    24	 * (a missing baseline would let a later run downgrade), and only warns if the follow-up status
    25	 * update fails (the ref is already recorded, which is what the guard reads).
    26	 */
    27	import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process'
    28	import semver from 'semver'
    29	
    30	// vX.Y.Z with an optional -rc.N or -hotfix.N suffix (matches the repo tag rulesets).
    31	const VERSION_TAG = /^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$/
    32	
    33	const [mode, env, ref] = process.argv.slice(2)
    34	const repo = process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY
    35	
    36	const die = (msg) => {
    37	    console.error(`✗ version-guard: ${msg}`)
    38	    process.exit(1)
    39	}
    40	const pass = (msg) => {
    41	    console.log(`✓ version-guard: ${msg}`)
    42	    process.exit(0)
    43	}
    44	
    45	if (!['check', 'record'].includes(mode) || !env || !ref) {
    46	    die('usage: versionGuard.mjs <check|record> <env> <ref>')
    47	}
    48	if (!repo) die('GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set')
    49	
    50	/** Run `gh` and return stdout. Optional `input` is written to stdin. Throws on non-zero exit. */
    51	function gh(args, input) {
    52	    return execFileSync('gh', args, {encoding: 'utf8', input})
    53	}
    54	
    55	/**
    56	 * Newest deployment ref for `env` that is a valid version tag, or null. Throws on API error.
    57	 * Pages through deployments (newest-first) so a long run of non-version (branch) deploys can't bury
    58	 * the last tag record. Skips non-version refs; fails closed if a version-shaped ref is not valid
    59	 * semver (so a malformed baseline like `v01.2.3` can't crash the compare or slip a downgrade through).
    60	 */
    61	function currentDeployedTag() {
    62	    const MAX_PAGES = 20 // 20 x 100 = 2000 deployments of headroom
    63	    for (let page = 1; page <= MAX_PAGES; page++) {
    64	        const out = gh([
    65	            'api',
    66	            `repos/${repo}/deployments?environment=${env}&per_page=100&page=${page}`,
    67	            '--jq',
    68	            '[.[].ref]'
    69	        ])
    70	        const refs = JSON.parse(out.trim() || '[]')
    71	        if (refs.length === 0) break // no more pages
    72	        for (const r of refs) {
    73	            if (!VERSION_TAG.test(r)) continue // skip branches / develop / other non-version refs
    74	            if (!semver.valid(r)) die(`stored deployment ref '${r}' for '${env}' is not valid semver — failing closed`)
    75	            return r // newest valid version tag
    76	        }
    77	    }
    78	    return null
    79	}
    80	
    81	const detail = (err) => String(err.stderr || err.message).trim().slice(0, 160)
    82	
    83	if (mode === 'check') {
    84	    if (!VERSION_TAG.test(ref)) pass(`'${ref}' is not a version tag — skipping downgrade check`)
    85	    if (!semver.valid(ref)) die(`'${ref}' is not valid semver`)
    86	
    87	    let current
    88	    try {
    89	        current = currentDeployedTag()
    90	    } catch (err) {
    91	        // Fail closed: if we cannot determine what is live, do not risk a downgrade.
    92	        die(`could not read deployments for '${env}' (failing closed): ${detail(err)}`)
    93	    }
    94	
    95	    if (current === null) pass(`no prior version tag on '${env}' — first deploy, allowing ${ref}`)
    96	    if (semver.lt(ref, current)) {
    97	        die(`refusing downgrade on '${env}': ${ref} is older than the live ${current}`)
    98	    }
    99	    pass(`${ref} is not older than the live ${current} on '${env}' — allowed`)
   100	}
   101	
   102	if (mode === 'record') {
   103	    if (!VERSION_TAG.test(ref)) pass(`'${ref}' is not a version tag — nothing to record`)
   104	    if (!semver.valid(ref)) die(`'${ref}' is not valid semver — refusing to record it`)
   105	    const body = JSON.stringify({
   106	        ref,
   107	        environment: env,
   108	        auto_merge: false,
   109	        required_contexts: [],
   110	        description: `tag ${ref}`
   111	    })
   112	    let id
   113	    try {
   114	        id = gh(['api', `repos/${repo}/deployments`, '--input', '-', '--jq', '.id'], body).trim()
   115	    } catch (err) {
   116	        // A missing record lets a later run read an older tag and allow a downgrade — fail loudly.
   117	        die(`could not record the deployed tag for '${env}' — the guard baseline is now stale: ${detail(err)}`)
   118	    }
   119	    try {
   120	        gh([
   121	            'api',
   122	            `repos/${repo}/deployments/${id}/statuses`,
   123	            '-f',
   124	            'state=success',
   125	            '-f',
   126	            `description=deployed ${ref}`
   127	        ])
   128	    } catch (err) {
   129	        // The ref is already recorded (that is what the guard reads); the status is cosmetic — warn only.
   130	        console.error(`::warning::version-guard: recorded deployment ${id} but could not set its status (${detail(err)})`)
   131	    }
   132	    pass(`recorded deployment ${id} for '${env}' = ${ref}`)
   133	}

    33	
    34	  bundle-size:
    35	    name: Bundle size check
    36	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    37	    continue-on-error: false
    38	    steps:
    39	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    40	
    41	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    42	        with:

    65	            exit 1
    66	          fi
    67	          echo "Dev gate: all checks passed"

    70	    name: Deploy to dev
    71	    needs: dev-gate

    77	      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}

     1	name: Deploy Test
     2	
     3	on:
     4	  workflow_dispatch:
     5	    inputs:
     6	      ref:
     7	        description: 'Branch or tag to deploy (e.g. feature/my-story, or a release tag)'
     8	        required: true
     9	        default: 'develop'
    10	      rollback:
    11	        description: 'Authorised rollback — skip the downgrade guard to deploy an older, known-good tag'
    12	        type: boolean
    13	        default: false
    14	
    15	permissions:
    16	  contents: read
    17	  id-token: write
    18	  deployments: write
    19	
    20	# Serialise deploys to this environment so two runs can't both pass the version
    21	# check and then land out of order (which would downgrade the environment).
    22	concurrency:
    23	  group: deploy-test
    24	  cancel-in-progress: false
    25	
    26	jobs:
    27	  deploy-test:
    28	    name: Deploy to Test
    29	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    30	    environment: test
    31	    outputs:
    32	      # Commit the deployed build was made from. The post-deploy gate pins to
    33	      # this so it measures the exact revision that landed on Test, even when
    34	      # `ref` is a mutable branch that moves between the two jobs' checkouts.
    35	      sha: ${{ steps.resolve-sha.outputs.sha }}
    36	    env:
    37	      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
    38	      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    39	    steps:
    40	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    41	        with:
    42	          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
    43	
    44	      - name: Resolve deployed commit SHA
    45	        id: resolve-sha
    46	        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    47	
    48	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    49	        with:
    50	          node-version: '24'
    51	          cache: 'npm'
    52	
    53	      - name: Install dependencies
    54	        run: npm install --include=dev
    55	
    56	      - name: Guard against version downgrade
    57	        if: ${{ inputs.rollback != true }}
    58	        env:
    59	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    60	          DEPLOY_REF: ${{ inputs.ref }}
    61	        run: node scripts/versionGuard.mjs check test "$DEPLOY_REF"
    62	
    63	      - name: Note authorised rollback (downgrade guard skipped)
    64	        if: ${{ inputs.rollback == true }}
    65	        env:
    66	          DEPLOY_REF: ${{ inputs.ref }}
    67	          ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
    68	        run: |
    69	          echo "::warning::Authorised rollback: downgrade guard skipped for '$DEPLOY_REF' on 'test' by '$ACTOR'; record still runs, so this tag becomes the new baseline."
    70	
    71	      - name: Push build to Test
    72	        run: npm run push:test
    73	
    74	      - name: Record deployed tag
    75	        if: success()
    76	        env:
    77	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    78	          DEPLOY_REF: ${{ inputs.ref }}
    79	        run: node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record test "$DEPLOY_REF"
    80	
    81	  # ── Post-deploy gate (deploy-then-gate) ─────────────────────────────────────
    82	  # Test is a fast disposable quick-look tier, so — unlike SIT's gate-then-deploy
    83	  # — we deploy first, then verify the same build here. This gate's overall
    84	  # pass/fail is the "safe to promote to SIT" signal.
    85	  #
    86	  # Currently bundle-size only. The P0 Playwright check attaches here once a
    87	  # *.p0.spec exists: add a `playwright-p0` job (mirroring digital-sit.yml,
    88	  # targeting the Test storefront via the `test` env's RETAIL_APP_HOME var),
    89	  # then list it in `test-gate.needs` and add its result to the check below.
    90	  bundle-size:
    91	    name: Bundle size check
    92	    needs: deploy-test
    93	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    94	    continue-on-error: false
    95	    steps:
    96	      # Pin to the exact commit deploy-test built, not the (mutable) input ref.
    97	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    98	        with:
    99	          ref: ${{ needs.deploy-test.outputs.sha }}
   100	
   101	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
   102	        with:
   103	          node-version: '24'
   104	          cache: 'npm'
   105	
   106	      - name: Install dependencies
   107	        run: npm install --include=dev
   108	
   109	      - name: Build and check bundle size
   110	        run: npm run test:max-file-size
   111	
   112	  test-gate:
   113	    name: Test Gate
   114	    needs: [deploy-test, bundle-size]
   115	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   116	    if: always()
   117	    steps:
   118	      - name: Check all Test gate signals passed
   119	        run: |
   120	          if [ "${{ needs.deploy-test.result }}" != "success" ] || \
   121	             [ "${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}" != "success" ]; then
   122	            echo "Test gate: one or more checks failed"
   123	            echo "  deploy-test:  ${{ needs.deploy-test.result }}"
   124	            echo "  bundle-size:  ${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}"
   125	            exit 1
   126	          fi

     5	# via the GitHub API, then PATCHes only the keys that are actually set
     6	# (non-empty) to the MRT target.
     7	#
     8	# Fallback order: target env value → shared env value → skip.
     9	# Keys that exist in .env.sample but are absent from both environments are
    10	# silently skipped — MRT retains whatever value it already holds for them.
    11	#

    13	# are not tagged mrt:true and are never included in the sync.

    15	# scope:personal and scope:auto keys (including ENVIRONMENT_NAME) are never
    16	# synced — they are developer-local or script-injected.
    17	#

    19	#     Production MRT env vars must be updated manually in the MRT console
    20	#     (runtime.commercecloud.com) by a tier-1-approver. This ensures prod
    21	#     changes go through a human gate rather than an automated workflow.
    22	#

    24	# Environment to propagate new values to MRT without a full redeploy.

    40	        description: 'Dry run — show what would be synced without calling MRT'
    41	        required: false
    42	        type: boolean
    43	        default: false
    44	
    45	permissions:

All three subagents are in. Here's the consolidated report.

---

# Zimmermann PWA — Process & Governance Playbook
*Read-only analysis, 2026-08-25, against `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`. Nothing was changed. Live GitHub state verified as `marcelannavarro` via `gh api`.*

## The six things that change how you operate today

1. **`prod`, `staging` and `uat` GitHub Environments have zero protection rules** (`gh api .../environments` → `{"name":"prod","protection":[]}`). `.claude/rules/tagging.md` states the `rollback=true` guard bypass "is not gated" until required reviewers exist. Verified: they still don't. Combined with `MRT_USER`/`MRT_API_KEY` living at **repo scope**, anyone with write access can `workflow_dispatch` `deploy-prod.yml` with any ref and no human gate.
2. **No `release/**` PR can merge today.** `SIT Gate` is a required check (`isAdminEnforced: true`, no bypass), and two of its four jobs cannot pass: `lighthouse-ci` needs `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`/`LHCI_TOKEN`/`LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` (none exist in repo or environment secrets), and `playwright-p0` runs `--project=p0` against **zero `*.p0.spec` files** with no `passWithNoTests`.
3. **`babel.config.js` and `tsconfig.json` are declared Tier 1 in `frozenFiles.md` and enforced nowhere** — absent from `CODEOWNERS` *and* from `protected-file-guard.yml`'s tier1 list. CODEOWNERS has no catch-all rule. `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, emits CSS on every page) is the same.
4. **Both required test checks on `develop` are conditional, and a skipped required check passes.** `qa.yml:211` and `qa.yml:240` gate on `detect-changes`, which diffs `since_last_remote_commit`. This already happened on PR #59 — the footer rewrite merged with Vitest, Storybook and both E2E jobs all reporting *skipping*.
5. **PDP ownership is contradicted across five artefacts**, and your current branch sits on it. `squadA.md:4` and `squadB.md:41` both say Squad A owns `pages/product-detail/`. `CODEOWNERS:162` and `protected-file-guard.yml:345` — the two that actually enforce — say **Squad B**.
6. **`sprintScope.md` is 61 days stale** and still says "Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)". Six skills cite it as authoritative.

---

# 1. Release, tagging and environment promotion

## Branch model
`AGENTS.md` Branch Rules + `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`. Verified live via GraphQL `branchProtectionRules`:

| Branch | Required checks | Approvals | Code-owner | Admin-enforced | Stale reviews dismissed | Conversation resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `develop` | `Unit tests (Vitest)`, `Storybook interaction & a11y tests`, `🔴 Branch Target Check` | 1 | yes | yes | **yes** | **no** |
| `main` | `🔴 Branch Target Check` **only** | 1 | yes | yes | **no** | **no** |
| `release/**` | `🔴 Branch Target Check`, `SIT Gate` | 1 | yes | yes | **no** | **no** |

`main` has **no test gate at all**, and `🔴 Branch Target Check` asserts exactly one thing (`protected-file-guard.yml:165`): `base == main && head == feature/*` → fail. A `release/*` → `main` PR passes it trivially. With `dismissesStaleReviews: false` and `requireLastPushApproval: false` on `main` and `release/**`, you can secure an approval then push anything before merging — the inverse of what you'd want.

Code fixes on a release go via `fix/release-{version}-{desc}` targeting the release branch (`releaseBranchesRules.md:34-46`); the forward-merge to `develop` happens through the release back-merge, never a separate PR (`:12,:36`).

## Tag taxonomy — who may cut what

| Pattern | Who | Verified enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | any developer | ruleset `tag-rc` (20487306), `bypass_actors: []` — `update`+`deletion` restricted **for everyone** |
| `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | tier-1-approvers only | ruleset `tag-release` (20487243), `creation` restricted, bypass = team id `18338648` = **`tier-1-approvers`** (confirmed) |

Both rulesets are `enforcement: active`. Their `tag_name_pattern` rules exist but `tagging.md` says they're Enterprise-only and inert on the Team plan — plausible and unfalsifiable read-only.

**Undocumented inversion:** `tag-release`'s bypass is `bypass_mode: always`, which covers *all* its rules — so a tier-1-approver **can delete or move a final `vX.Y.Z` tag**, while nobody can touch an `-rc.N`. That contradicts `tagging.md`'s "Every deployable version is an immutable, annotated git tag."

Only **one tag exists**: `v0.1.0-rc.0`. `package.json:version` is `0.0.1` (expected — bumped once at the final-release PR, since `npm version` is deliberately avoided; the bump commit would be blocked by `release/**` protection).

## The six environments

| Env | Trigger | Version guard | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` | push to `develop` (`deploy-dev.yml:3-6`) | none (by design) | `dev-gate` = contract-tests + bundle-size |
| `sit` | `workflow_run` off SIT Gate on `release/**` (`deploy-sit.yml:4-9`) | none (by design) | gate-then-deploy |
| `test` | `workflow_dispatch`, default `develop` | check+record | **deploy-then-gate** (`deploy-test.yml:81-89`); `bundle-size` pinned to the deployed SHA |
| `uat` | `workflow_dispatch`, **default `develop`** | check+record | |
| `staging` | `workflow_dispatch`, **default `main`** | check+record | file is `deploy-stg.yml`, environment is `staging`, MRT target is `staging` |
| `prod` | `workflow_dispatch`, ref required, no default | check+record | MRT target is **`production`** (`package.json:push:prod`) |

**A seventh surface exists and isn't in `tagging.md`'s environment model at all:** `deploy-preview.yml` auto-deploys ephemeral per-branch MRT previews on every push to `feature/**`/`fix/**` (excluding `fix/release-*`), bound to `environment: dev`. Both it and `teardown-preview.yml` were added 2026-08-19; `tagging.md` was last touched 2026-08-07 and its two-category table was never updated.

## Version guard behaviour (`scripts/versionGuard.mjs`)

`VERSION_TAG = /^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$/` (`:31`). Pages 20×100 deployments newest-first (`:62-77`) so branch deploys can't bury the last tag. Fails closed on lookup error (`:92`), on invalid stored ref (`:74`), and on non-semver input (`:85`). `record` fails the run if it can't write the baseline (`:117`).

**The hole is the skip path.** `check` *passes* on any non-version-tag ref (`:84`) and `record` *skips* it (`:103`). Since `deploy-uat.yml:9` defaults to `develop`, `deploy-stg.yml:9` defaults to `main`, and `deploy-prod.yml:7` explicitly advertises "Tag or branch", **a branch deploy to any tier bypasses the guard entirely and leaves no baseline** — so the guard's notion of what's live silently diverges from reality.

`rollback=true` skips `check` but still runs `record` (`if: success()`, no rollback condition), so the rolled-back tag becomes the new baseline — doc is accurate here. Its only gate is environment required reviewers, which **do not exist**.

## Tag naming enforcement, three layers
1. `scripts/hooks/pre-push:20-21` — prevention, bypassable via `--no-verify` or a clone where `prepare` never ran.
2. `tag-validate.yml:19-20` — post-hoc detection only, not a block.
3. Rulesets — immutability + tier-1-only final tags (real); naming inert on Team plan.

## Doc-vs-workflow disagreements
- `tagging.md` calls test/uat/staging/prod "tag-promoted / deliberate". **Three of the four default to a branch ref.**
- `tagging.md`'s environment table omits `deploy-preview.yml` entirely.
- `deploy-dev.yml:92-119`'s `tag-sprint` job diffs `scripts/sprint.txt` — **that file does not exist and never has**. The job is permanently dead.
- `test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0` (`package.json:85`). The "MuleSoft contract tests" job in both `deploy-dev.yml:32` and `digital-sit.yml:116` always passes vacuously, and `sit-gate:144-147` counts that as a real signal.
- `package.json:57` runs `lhci autorun --config=tests/lighthouserc.js`; `tests/` doesn't exist. The real file is `./lighthouserc.js`. `AGENTS.md:37` and `protected-file-guard.yml:82` both name the stale path; `CODEOWNERS:61` covers the real one.
- `.docs/architecture.md:91,108` still lists a 5-tier topology with no Test and MRT target `stage`. Stale.

## What bites you — release
1. **A branch ref silently disarms the downgrade guard on prod.** One click on `deploy-prod.yml` with `develop` and the guard logs a green "not a version tag — skipping."
2. **After any branch deploy, the guard's baseline is a lie.** It will later block a genuinely-newer tag against a stale recorded tag while the environment actually runs something else. Re-run `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod <tag>` after any out-of-band deploy.
3. **`rollback=true` is a real, ungated bypass right now.** Setting required reviewers on `prod`/`staging`/`uat` is the single highest-value fix in this whole report.
4. **`main` is the least-protected branch in the repo.** No tests, no stale-review dismissal.
5. **The SIT gate cannot pass** — no LHCI secrets, no `*.p0.spec`. Discover this the week you cut `release/v0.1.0` and you're blocked on secrets provisioning, not code.
6. **Three-way name divergence:** GitHub Environment (`staging`/`prod`) ≠ workflow file (`stg`/`prod`) ≠ MRT target (`staging`/`production`). Tooling must key off the GitHub Environment name; `versionGuard.mjs` does.
7. **An unrelated Pages-publish failure blocks the SIT deploy.** `deploy-sit.yml:18` keys off `workflow_run.conclusion`, which is the *whole workflow's* result — including `deploy-playwright-report` (`digital-sit.yml:55-66`, `if: always()`).
8. **Final release tags are mutable for tier-1-approvers; RC tags are immutable for everyone.**

---

# 2. Protection tiers and approval

## What makes a tier
- **Tier 1** (`frozenFiles.md`) — design foundations, the 7 Commerce SDK hooks, runtime/integration config, build pipeline, test/tooling config, CI/CD, governance. Requires the developer to name the file in-prompt + owner approval, *unless* the verified-gh-identity exception applies. **`ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` are absolute** — `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule #4 says the exception never applies to them.
- **Tier 2** (`protectedFiles.md`) — shared shell, shared product/commerce components, theme component styles, translations, 5+-consumer hooks, env tooling, Contentful schema. Needs a second reviewer.
- **Tier 3** (`CODEOWNERS:150-186`) — plain squad ownership, explicitly *not* a protection gate.

## How approval is actually enforced
Server-side, and it works: `require_code_owner_reviews: true` + `enforce_admins: true` + `bypass_pull_request_allowances: []` on all three protected branches. All five CODEOWNERS teams **exist and have members** (tier-1: 3, tier-2: 2, squad-a: 2, squad-b: 2, qa: 6) — no silently-ignored lines.

Advisory only: `tier1-guard` (deliberately not required — `protected-file-guard.yml:24-37` documents GitHub's Feb-2025 cross-run check-run lockdown as the reason), `tier2-warning`, `cross-squad-guard`, `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh`, and Claude's own confirmation prompt.

## Three-way drift: `frozenFiles.md` / `protectedFiles.md` vs `CODEOWNERS` vs `protected-file-guard.yml`

| Path | Declared tier | CODEOWNERS | CI guard list |
|---|---|---|---|
| `babel.config.js` | **Tier 1** | **absent** | **absent** |
| `tsconfig.json` | **Tier 1** | **absent** | **absent** |
| `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` | **Tier 2** | **absent** | **absent** |
| `overrides/app/ssr/**` (CSP, SLAS) | Tier 1 | `:46` ✓ | **absent** — guard uses `overrides/app/ssr.*` (`:73`), a literal dot that cannot match `ssr/slasTokens.ts` |
| `vitest.setup.ts` | Tier 1 | `:57` ✓ | absent |
| `.browserstack.yml` | Tier 1 | `:60` ✓ | absent |
| `config/countries.ts`, `config/contentful.ts` | Tier 1 | `:47-48` ✓ | absent |
| `uiCopyProvider/` | Tier 2 | `:93` ✓ | absent |
| `switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/*` | Tier 2 | `:139,146-148` ✓ | absent |
| `package-lock.json` | not listed | absent | `:77` — guard is *broader* here |

The `CODEOWNERS`-absent rows are the real holes; the guard-absent rows only lose the warning banner. **CODEOWNERS has no catch-all `*` rule** (verified across all 190 lines), so a path absent from it requires zero code-owner review regardless of what the rules files say.

Also ungated by anything: `scripts/versionGuard.mjs` (the entire downgrade-protection mechanism), `.husky/*` (the one-line shims that *invoke* the gated `scripts/hooks/` content — empty one and the gated hook is disabled with no review), `.env.sample`, `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`.

## Last-match-wins
One deliberate override exists: `CODEOWNERS:186` `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, placed last among the `components/` rules. It downgrades any co-located style file inside a Tier 2 directory. Live instances today: the three `footer/**/*.css.ts` files. Documented at `:178-186`, `overrideStyling.md`, `protectedFiles.md:61` — and `overrideStyling.md` itself flags it as an **open governance question**, since `zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated. No *accidental* silent overrides found.

## The squad contradiction
`squadA.md:4-5,33-35` claims `pages/home/`, `product-detail/`, `product-list/` for Squad A, and `squadB.md:41` agrees. Against that: `CODEOWNERS:161-163` (squad-b), `protected-file-guard.yml:344-346` (`squad_b`), `coderabbit.yaml:301-314` ("SQUAD B — PDP", "SQUAD B — PLP"), and four skills. **The enforcing artefacts say Squad B.** `squadA.md` is headed "Draft squad split" and hasn't been touched since 2026-07-14.

## Your current branch, concretely
Computed against CODEOWNERS' last-match-wins:
- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` → `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers` (only 2 and 3 people respectively)
- `overrides/app/routes.tsx` → squad-a + squad-b + tier-2 + tier-1
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**` → **`@pwa-squad-b`** (despite `squadA.md`)
- `ui-kits/**` → squad-a + squad-b
- **No code owner at all**: `components/product-view/index.tsx`, `types/vendor.d.ts`, `utils/richText.tsx`, `utils/richText.test.tsx`

## What bites you — tiers
1. **`.claude/rules/` is documentation; `CODEOWNERS` is configuration.** When you want to know what will actually block, read CODEOWNERS. Teach this at onboarding.
2. **Editing `tsconfig.json` — strict mode and every path alias — needs no approval from anyone.**
3. **A CSP change in `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` produces a silent PR.** CODEOWNERS catches it; the loud red banner a reviewer looks for does not fire.
4. **New shared design-system atoms land in `ui-kits/`, which is Tier 3** — one squad's approval, no tier gate, for components both squads consume.
5. **A `.css.ts` inside `_app-config/` or `seo/` would drop the Tier 2 gate** the same way the footer files do. Nothing prevents it.
6. **The named owners in the rules files ("UI Designer", "Integration / SI Partner") don't exist as GitHub teams** — `CODEOWNERS:115-116,120-121,138,144-145` admits the fallback to generic approver pools.
7. **`tier-2-approvers` has 2 members and `tier-1-approvers` has 3.** Any PR touching `theme/components/` is a two-person bus factor.

---

# 3. PR and review workflow

## Mechanically enforced at PR time
- Three required checks on `develop` (above). **`Playwright E2E (localhost)` and `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` are required nowhere** — they can be red and the PR merges. `teardown-preview.yml` reported `fail` on PR #59 and it merged.
- `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` gates everything via `since_last_remote_commit: true` (`:72`) — diffed against the previous push, not the merge base. The file's own comment at `:22-23` acknowledges *"GitHub treats a skipped required check as passing."*

## CodeRabbit — advisory as a check, blocking as a reviewer
`request_changes_workflow: true` (`coderabbit.yaml:32`) + `requiredApprovingReviewCount: 1` means a *Changes requested* review blocks the merge button. But the `CodeRabbit` status check is in no required-context list, so its `mode: error` pre-merge checks (`:399-430`) don't block that way. On `develop`, only `HardiAcn` can dismiss reviews.

Two switches that turn it off invisibly: `ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]` (`:391-393`) is **title-matched, not author-matched**, and `drafts: false` (`:389`). Neither shows as a failing check — it just goes quiet.

`code_guidelines.filePatterns` (`:462-465`) loads literal file content and **does not follow AGENTS.md's markdown links** — `overrideStyling.md` and `tagging.md` are not in the list and are therefore invisible to review.

## Rule blind spots worth knowing
All three ast-grep rules are `severity: warning`. Both semgrep rules are `ERROR`.
- `img-missing-alt` matches `^img$` only — **`<Image>`, the idiomatic Chakra element, is invisible.**
- `icon-button-missing-aria-label`'s `^aria-label\b` **does not match `aria-labelledby`** (word boundary fails on the following `l`) — the more correct answer gets flagged.
- `clickable-non-interactive-element` accepts `role="presentation"`/`role="none"`, and checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown` despite `components.md` requiring both.
- `payment-credential-logged` sinks are only `console.*` and `Sentry.*` — `dataLayer.push`, `localStorage.setItem`, a logger, a query string and a response body all pass. Sources exclude `let`/`var`, property access and destructuring; the name list misses **`cvc`**.
- `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` only excludes an *inline* `.sanitize()`. The idiomatic `const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` then `{{__html: clean}}` is **reported as an ERROR**, while a spread-props form evades entirely.

## Git hooks — all best-effort
`pre-commit` (324 lines) regenerates the registry, syncs derived AI configs, regenerates Contentful definitions, **blocks** direct edits to derived config, and **blocks** `.env.sample` commits with secret-shaped values. **It runs no lint, no `tsc`, no tests.** `commit-msg` enforces conventional commits with a lowercase scope. `pre-push` validates `v*` tag names. All defeated by `--no-verify` or `npm install --ignore-scripts`.

## No CI gate at all
`npm run lint` · `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run audit:tokens` (14 untriaged pre-existing violations) · `npm run format` (globs `**/*.{js,jsx}`, so it never touches `overrides/`'s TypeScript) · `sync:ai-rules:check` · **test coverage** (`vitest.config.ts` has no coverage block). Bundle size and Lighthouse exist but only post-merge or at release tier.

## Human-only
Running `cr review --light --base develop` before every non-trivial commit (AGENTS.md calls it "required, not optional" — nothing verifies it). Replying in-thread to every CodeRabbit finding — **`requiresConversationResolution: false` on all three branches**, so nothing blocks a merge with every thread unanswered. Pasting the Jira URL into the PR body. The copy-first override protocol.

## What bites you — PR
1. **A docs-only final commit turns both required gates green.** Read the *history* of check runs on a PR, not the head SHA's current state. "skipping" means unverified, not passed — and if an earlier push failed unit tests, a docs commit flips the required check to green.
2. **`detect-changes` failing green-lights the PR.** The most load-bearing job in the pipeline is not itself required.
3. **A header-only change gets the narrowest E2E scope despite the widest blast radius** — `e2e_homepage` includes `components/header/**`.
4. **`chore(deps):` in a human PR title disables CodeRabbit entirely** — no semgrep, no ast-grep, no gitleaks.
5. **The semgrep XSS rule flags the correct pattern and misses the dangerous one.** Your team will learn to ignore it. When you dismiss one, reply in-thread with the reason or CodeRabbit re-raises it forever.
6. **Renaming a `qa.yml` job breaks merging repo-wide** — required contexts match by display name; the check would sit "Expected" forever. And `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1.
7. **`e2e-browserstack` uses `always()` (`qa.yml:433`) while the comment above it claims parity with `e2e-localhost`'s `!cancelled()` (`:314`)** — superseded pushes burn paid BrowserStack sessions.
8. **`CODERABBIT_API_KEY` is a live 61-char credential stored as a plaintext GitHub Actions *variable*** in the `shared` and `dev` environments — readable via the API by anyone with repo read, and unmasked in logs. It should be a secret.
